summary: Verified /sponsorship-documents.zip served from frontend public URL against all 8 checks in the review request. 7/8 passed. One failure: 5 Metro Bank Statement PDFs do not start with the %PDF magic bytes at offset 0 (they have leading whitespace/newline before the header).

minor.issue: 5 PDFs inside the ZIP do not start with '%PDF' magic bytes at byte 0. Files: 'Bank Statements/Metro Bank Statement {Feb/Mar/May/Jun} 2026.pdf' have 332 bytes of leading ASCII spaces before '%PDF'; 'Bank Statements/Metro Bank Statement Jan 2026.pdf' has 1 leading '\n' byte. pypdf still parses them (17-19 pages each) with warnings ('invalid pdf header'). This is a defect in the source Metro Bank statement PDFs themselves (not introduced by the ZIP rebuild) but violates the review request assertion 'starts with %PDF magic bytes'. Strict PDF viewers and some Windows preview handlers may reject these.

action_items: Sanitize the 5 Metro Bank Statement PDFs so their %PDF header is at byte 0. Simplest fix: strip leading whitespace bytes before the first '%PDF' occurrence, or re-encode via `qpdf --linearize input.pdf output.pdf` / `gs -o out.pdf -sDEVICE=pdfwrite in.pdf` and then re-inject into the ZIP. Once fixed, all 8 assertions will pass.

rca of the issue: RCA: The Metro Bank Statement PDFs were pre-existing source files uploaded by the user (part of the original 43MB archive). Metro Bank's PDF statement generator (or an intermediate tool) prepends whitespace before the %PDF header — 332 spaces for Feb/Mar/May/Jun 2026, one newline for Jan 2026. The ZIP rebuild script (/tmp/sponsorship_work/rebuild_windows_safe.sh) preserved these files byte-for-byte, so the defect flowed through. Mitigation: Add a sanitization pass before zipping — for every *.pdf, locate first '%PDF' occurrence with data.find(b'%PDF') and rewrite the file starting from that offset (or run through qpdf/gs to re-linearize). Then reflow the ZIP.
